findings.title: PW-004 unplanned outage (2026-07-29T02:00–08:00Z) with no replay swallowed eight candidates across four automations
findings.cause: The orchestrator cluster was offline for the whole of PW-004 and performed no replay on recovery. For each of these eight, the moment the condition first satisfied its own automation's definition falls strictly inside 2026-07-29T02:00:00Z–08:00:00Z, so the event-driven platform had no live trigger and never revisited them. ASOP-114 P-104 qualified at 03:05 (entered 02:35 + 30 min) and P-110 at 03:50 (03:20 + 30); ASOP-233 T-04 qualified at 02:55 (02:25 + 30) and T-20 at 04:10 (03:40 + 30), both unscheduled RC-ALARM; ASOP-402 C-018 qualified at 02:40 (due 02:10 + 30 grace) and C-050 at 06:50 (due 06:20 + 30 grace); ASOP-207 B-8804 and B-8810 had their latest moving event posted at 02:50 and 04:15 with remaining time already negative. All four intervals that close (06:05, 06:28, 05:55, 06:05) also close before the platform returned at 08:00, so no post-recovery edge existed either.
evidence: PW-004: status "down", window_start "2026-07-29T02:00:00Z", window_end "2026-07-29T08:00:00Z", note "Unplanned outage. Orchestrator cluster offline for 6h. No replay of missed candidates on recovery."
Every one of these eight rows carries "platform_status": "down"

findings.title: Maintenance-mode bypass stood down both port automations as designed
findings.cause: ASOP-114 and ASOP-118 share one bypass clause, port_mode = 'maint': a port under maintenance is not dispatched to. Both candidates were attributed that bypass and both occurred while the platform was up, so the stand-down — not any platform or query defect — is what accounts for each silence individually. P-106 exceeded the 30-minute blocked threshold (145 min) and P-114 exceeded the 15-minute error threshold (58 min); each condition genuinely occurred and was deliberately not actioned.
evidence: ASOP-114 bypass: name "maintenance mode", clause "port_mode = 'maint'", note "A port under maintenance is not dispatched to. Explains the silence; the block still happened."
ASOP-118 bypass note: "Same bypass as ASOP-114, and it is the only thing these two share besides the table."

findings.title: ASOP-233 T-23 fell between the retired 60-minute threshold and the current 30-minute threshold
findings.cause: The deployed detection appears still to be running the pre-revision threshold. T-23 was down 38 unscheduled minutes: it qualifies under the configured thresholdMinutes of 30 but not under the 60 minutes recorded in thresholdHistory as revised on 2026-05-14. The platform was nominal and no bypass applied, so a stale threshold value is the only condition consistent with the automation's definition that leaves this candidate unselected.

findings.title: Engineering holds are backfilled from the engineering queue, so ASOP-341 stayed quiet
findings.cause: Both holds carry hold_type = 'engineering', which is ASOP-341's bypass clause: engineering holds are backfilled from the engineering queue rather than dispatched here. ASOP-341 has no window, no threshold and no platform-status join, so timing plays no part for either row; the bypass alone accounts for each.

findings.title: Material hold H-3359 was placed inside the PW-004 outage and never re-triggered
findings.cause: H-3359 carries no bypass and is a plain unassigned-department hold, so nothing in the automation's definition excuses it. Its only trigger event — the hold insert at 2026-07-29T05:30:00Z — falls inside the PW-004 outage, and the platform is event-driven with no historical replay, so the candidate was lost. Kept separate from the main outage finding because ASOP-341 has joinsPlatformStatus false and the row carries no platform_status attribution; the link rests on placed_at alone, and ASOP-341's "every row in the table is evaluated" wording leaves open whether a later evaluation should have picked it up (the hold stayed unassigned until released_at 2026-07-30T01:17:00Z).

findings.title: Recorded skip reasons suppressed two missed checks
findings.cause: Both checks came due inside the window, the 30-minute grace elapsed, ran_at is absent and both tools are inside the production-bay constriction — but each carries a non-null skip_reason, which is ASOP-402's bypass. The platform was nominal for both, so the recorded skip is the whole explanation for each; as the bypass note says, a reason explains why the check went unrun, it does not make it run.

findings.title: Hard-bounce 550 suppressed three retry escalations
findings.cause: All three messages exceeded the attemptCeiling of 3 and were never acknowledged, but each carries bounce_code '550', ASOP-455's hard-bounce bypass: the address is dead so retry escalation was deliberately suppressed. ASOP-455 has timePredicate "none" and joinsPlatformStatus false, so platform availability is irrelevant to all three; the bypass accounts for each on its own.

findings.title: Two ASOP-207 deadline warnings unexplained; both had their latest moving event recorded only after the deadline had passed
findings.cause: No cause in the bundle accounts for these. Both qualify squarely — latest event is a moving state, minutes_remaining is below the 60-minute warning threshold — ASOP-207 has no constrictions and no bypasses, and both occurred while the platform was nominal. They are grouped only because they share the single distinguishing pattern available: the most recent event for the (batch_id, step_id) was timestamped after queue_deadline had already elapsed (18:18 vs 18:00; 02:24 vs 02:15), i.e. there was no in-window event for an event-driven platform to react to during the countdown. That is a hypothesis the bundle does not confirm, so the misses are recorded as unexplained rather than attributed to a logic gap.

findings.title: ASOP-455 M-0062 unexplained: over the ceiling, no hard bounce, platform nominal
findings.cause: No supportable cause. M-0062 has attempts 4 against an attemptCeiling of 3, was never acknowledged, and bounce_code is "timeout" so the hard-bounce bypass does not apply; ASOP-455 has no time predicate and does not join platform status, so the outage and degraded windows are irrelevant. The only observation worth recording is that 4 is exactly ceiling+1 — the minimum qualifying value, and the lowest attempt count among the four ASOP-455 candidates (11, 9, 5, 4) — which would be consistent with a boundary error in the deployed comparison, but the bundle contains no evidence of how the comparison is written.
evidence: Row: message_id "M-0062", attempts 4, "bounce_code": "timeout", "bypass": null, queued_at "2026-07-23T08:57:00Z", sent_at "2026-07-23T09:17:00Z"
ASOP-455 configs: "attemptCeiling": 3, acknowledgementColumn "acked_at", "timePredicate": "none"
Bypass clause is "bounce_code = '550'"; this row's bounce_code is "timeout"

notes: Two data observations that did not rise to findings. (1) The ASOP-118 row for P-114 carries no port_mode column at all (it has "unit_present": 0 instead) yet the pass attributed "bypass": "port_mode = maint"; the maintenance grouping therefore rests on the attribution rather than on a visible port_mode value in that row. (2) All four ASOP-207 rows have "next_tool_group": null, including the two explained by the PW-004 outage, so that null does not discriminate the unexplained pair and was not used as a cause. Also noted: PW-002 (2026-07-26T03:30–05:10Z, degraded, "dispatcher unaffected") and PW-006 (2026-08-02T23:00–2026-08-03T00:15Z, degraded) contain no misses and explain none.
